content: Each interaction is addressed individually: 1. Ethynodiol/Ethinyl Estradiol Usage: Take the active hormonal tablets for 21 days, followed by 7 days of either inert tablets or no tablets. Repeat this cycle. Follow the manufacturer’s color-coding to distinguish active from inert tablets. Begin the regimen on the first day of the menstrual cycle or the Sunday following the start of menstruation. 2. Postpartum Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Risk: Combined hormonal contraceptives increase the risk of VTE after delivery. This risk decreases significantly after 21 days but does not normalize until 42 days postpartum. The CDC recommends waiting 3–6 weeks postpartum before initiating combined hormonal contraceptives in women without additional VTE risk factors. After vaginal delivery: Wait at least 3 weeks. After cesarean section: Wait at least 6 weeks. Women with additional VTE risk factors: Avoid combined hormonal contraceptives entirely. 3. Fezolinetant Interaction: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels and effects of fezolinetant by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir/Dasabuvir Interaction: Co-administration with ethinyl estradiol can cause significant ALT elevations (>5x ULN, sometimes >20x ULN). Discontinue ethinyl estradiol-containing medications before starting this hepatitis C regimen. Restart ethinyl estradiol approximately 2 weeks after completing the treatment. 5. Tranexamic Acid Interaction: Co-administration with ethinyl estradiol increases thrombotic risk due to pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Amobarbital Interaction: Amobarbital reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use an alternative drug or nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 7. Anastrozole Interaction: Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use of anastrozole with any estrogen-containing products. 8. Apalutamide Interaction: Apalutamide decreases the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, monitor for reduced therapeutic effects and adjust doses as needed. 9. Armodafinil Interaction: Armodafinil decreases the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 10. Atazanavir Interaction: Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur with atazanavir. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Use alternative nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 11. Belzutifan Interaction: Belzutifan reduces the efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding. Advise women to use effective nonhormonal contraception. Belzutifan may also cause fetal harm based on animal studies. 12. Bosentan Interaction: Bosentan reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 13. Brigatinib Interaction: Brigatinib reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. Brigatinib may cause fetal harm. 14. Butabarbital Interaction: Butabarbital reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 15. Calaspargase Pegol Interaction: Due to potential indirect interactions, avoid using calaspargase pegol with oral contraceptives. Use alternative non-oral contraceptive methods. 16. Carbamazepine Interaction: Carbamazepine reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 17. Conivaptan Interaction: Conivaptan increases the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 18. Dexamethasone Interaction: Dexamethasone reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 19. Efavirenz Interaction: Efavirenz reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 20. Elagolix Interaction: Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of elagolix through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Women should use nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for 1 week after discontinuing elagolix. 21. Elvitegravir Interaction: Elvitegravir reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by an unknown mechanism. Use alternative nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 22. Enasidenib Interaction: Enasidenib increases the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol. Avoid co-administration with sensitive substrates of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP. If unavoidable, adjust substrate dosages accordingly. 23. Encorafenib Interaction: Encorafenib reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Women should use highly effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for 2 weeks after the final dose. Encorafenib may cause fetal harm. 24. Enoxaparin Interaction: Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of enoxaparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 25. Enzalutamide Interaction: Enzalutamide reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternative drugs or nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 26. Eslcarbazepine Acetate Interaction: Eslcarbazepine acetate reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use additional or alternative nonhormonal birth control methods. 27. Exemestane Interaction: Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of exemestane through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use with estrogen-containing products. 28. Fedratinib Interaction: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels and effects of fedratinib. Avoid co-administration with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors. 29. Fexinidazole Interaction: Fexinidazole increases the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 30. Fosamprenavir Interaction: Co-administration with ethinyl estradiol may alter hormone levels and reduce contraceptive efficacy. Use alternative nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 31. Griseofulvin Interaction: Griseofulvin reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 32. Heparin Interaction: Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of heparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 33. Idelalisib Interaction: Idelalisib increases the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 34. Indinavir Interaction: Indinavir increases the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 35. Isavuconazonium Sulfate Interaction: Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 36. Ivosidenib Interaction: Ivosidenib reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or monitor for therapeutic loss if unavoidable. 37. Leniolisib Interaction: Leniolisib increases the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 38. Lesinurad Interaction: Lesinurad reduces the efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 39. Letrozole Interaction: Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of letrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use with estrogen-containing products. 40. Lonafarnib Interaction: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels and effects of lonafarnib. Monitor for arrhythmias and other cardiac events if co-administration is unavoidable. 41. Lopinavir Interaction: Lopinavir increases the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 42. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor Interaction: Lumacaftor/ivacaftor reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable during co-administration. Use alternative nonhormonal methods. 43. Mavacamten Interaction: Mavacamten reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraceptive methods during treatment and for 4 months after the last dose. 44. Metyrapone Interaction: Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of metyrapone. Discontinue estrogens prior to and during metyrapone administration. 45. Mifepristone Interaction: Mifepristone increases the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 46. Mycophenolate Interaction: Mycophenolate reduces the efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by an unknown mechanism. Use alternative or additional contraceptive methods. 47. Nelfinavir Interaction: Nelfinavir increases the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 48. Nevirapine Interaction: Nevirapine reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraceptive methods.
